scope: Authoritative user-supplied intended architecture briefs and uncompleted production targets. This does not describe or certify the existing workshop assets, active renderer, gameplay sect doctrines or published settings.

technicalArtStandard.heading: Required technical art standard
paragraphs: Every architectural sprite must use a single consistent shallow three-quarter perspective, with a clear view of the roof and front façade. The lighting direction, outline thickness, pixel density, shadow treatment and material palettes must match across the entire project.

Buildings must be authored as properly scaled sprites, while complete settlements are assembled from independent parts aligned to the game's world grid. A multi-building sect must never be flattened into one small hall sprite.

At minimum, every sect type requires a principal hall, residential architecture, specialty structures, entrance structures, environmental decorations and functional navigation assets. Large landmarks such as mountains, enormous trees and waterfalls require their own world-aligned layers.
Individual sprites require transparent backgrounds and carefully defined ground anchors. Foundations must meet the real terrain. Large decorative masses cannot conceal traversable roads or entrances.

Every design should support at least two meaningful architectural variations, plus settlement-growth variations. These must change shapes, arrangements and construction details rather than merely adjusting colours.

Final quality requirement: When shown without colour, the Citadel, Sky Monastery, Canopy Village, River Delta and all other sects must still be recognisably different. When shown in the actual game at ordinary zoom, roofs, entrances, streets, major structures and characters must remain visually coherent.
These are the intended designs—not a claim that the existing workshop assets already meet the specification.

registry.name: Canopy Village
registry.identity: An elevated woodland civilization living within enormous ancient trees.
registry.landmark: The main hall occupies a massive living tree with several accessible levels, a broad ceremonial platform, curved wooden galleries and lookout balconies.
registry.supportingStructures: Supporting sprites include branch houses, tree shrines, suspended gardens, rope lanterns, lookout nests and platforms supported by roots.
registry.terrain: The terrain is a dense old-growth forest with varied tree sizes, natural clearings, roots and understory vegetation. Rope bridges, reinforced wooden walkways and trunk staircases connect the elevated buildings.
registry.palette: Deep forest green, rich brown wood, moss, golden lanterns and subdued natural fabrics.
registry.signatureSilhouette: The signature silhouette is towering living trees carrying an interconnected village, never simple box houses with round green circles behind them.
additionalArchitecture: Buildings are genuinely integrated into gigantic trunks and branches. Their floors wrap around trees, and some homes hang beneath immense limbs. Curved leaf-covered roofs, open timber balconies, woven walls and carved wooden doorframes create a natural architectural language.

registry.name: Step Pyramid
registry.identity: A ceremonial civilization centred on a monumental stepped temple.
registry.landmark: The main structure is a broad terraced pyramid with precisely cut stone blocks, recessed ceremonial chambers, carved relief panels and a large sanctuary at the summit.
registry.supportingStructures: Small corner shrines, priests' quarters, sacrificial or ceremonial altars, enclosed courtyards and stone monuments surround the pyramid.
registry.terrain: The terrain is a dry, elevated rocky mesa. The pyramid dominates an axial settlement in which roads and ceremonial squares align directly with its main staircase.
registry.palette: Sandstone, ochre, terracotta and turquoise ornamentation.
registry.signatureSilhouette: The silhouette is a massive stepped pyramid with broad central stairs, surrounded by smaller structures.
materialDetails: Stone edges show age, cracks and erosion.

registry.name: Cliff Dwellings
registry.identity: A civilization that has carved its architecture directly into enormous limestone cliffs.
registry.landmark: The main hall is recessed into a sheer rock face with giant arched entrances, multiple tiers of carved balconies and exposed timber galleries.
registry.supportingStructures: Smaller structures consist of cave residences, lookout openings, stone-cut chambers, hanging balconies, bridge supports and tunnel entrances.
registry.terrain: The cliff itself forms the dominant architecture. A web of stairways, rock galleries and internal passage entrances connects residential clusters on different elevations.
registry.palette: Pale limestone, brown timber, dusty cream stone, worn bronze ornaments and shaded interior doorways.
registry.signatureSilhouette: The silhouette must show buildings embedded inside a vertical mountain wall, rather than houses sitting in front of it.

registry.name: Crystal Spires
registry.identity: An elegant cultivation settlement built among giant natural crystal formations.
registry.landmark: The main sanctuary features an enormous central crystal spire enclosed by a partially open stone structure.

materialDetails: Crystals have controlled internal colour facets and sharp, readable edges.

registry.name: River Delta
registry.identity: A thriving river civilization built across numerous islands and waterways.
registry.landmark: The main hall is an expansive timber pavilion on heavy wooden stilts, with broad layered roofs, open verandas, carved supporting posts and a large dock beneath or beside it.
registry.supportingStructures: Supporting buildings include smaller stilt residences, storehouses, boat sheds, fishing platforms, river shrines, covered docks and watch platforms.
registry.terrain: The environment consists of naturally branching river channels, islands of different sizes, muddy banks, reeds, stones and shallow-water vegetation. Wooden bridges and broad boardwalks connect the settlement.
registry.palette: Weathered amber timber, dark teak beams, moss-green and straw-coloured roofing, blue-green water and warm lanterns.
registry.signatureSilhouette: The signature silhouette is an interconnected waterfront settlement with visibly supported buildings, never two huts on a rectangular blue patch.

registry.name: Watch Fortress
registry.identity: A defensive frontier sect specializing in surveillance and territorial protection.
registry.landmark: Unlike the enclosed Citadel, this architecture is distributed along a long, uneven ridgeline. The dominant features are tall observation towers with exposed lookout platforms, reinforced bases, narrow defensive windows and signal beacons.
registry.supportingStructures: Buildings include small barracks, fortified patrol houses, gate posts, supply depots and a command keep positioned above the surrounding landscape.
registry.terrain: A continuous patrol route connects lookout towers along the ridge. Defensive paths and low parapets follow natural contours.
registry.palette: Cool grey stone, dark timber, iron reinforcement and military-coloured banners.
registry.signatureSilhouette: The silhouette is a chain of tall observation towers distributed along a ridge.
